## Purpose

`mlmr` provides an open, reproducible graphical and programmatic toolkit for the
multilevel models most widely taught and published in education, psychology,
public health, and organizational research—running natively on `lme4` with
inspectable R scripts.

## Multilevel Capabilities Matrix

`mlm_feature_matrix()` summarizes 25 capabilities across model specification,
centering, live symbolic equations, empirical Bayes intercept and slope
reliabilities, cluster-robust sandwich standard errors, multiparameter Wald
hypothesis tests, variance-component likelihood-ratio tests, Level-1 variance
homogeneity testing, residual exports, and generalized mixed-model marginal
effects:

```{r capabilities, eval = TRUE}
knitr::kable(mlmr::mlm_feature_matrix())
```

## Inferential and Diagnostic Estimators

The exported companion functions implement standard multilevel estimators
directly from the fitted `lme4` mixed-model blocks (Liang & Zeger, 1986;
Raudenbush & Bryk, 2002; Stram & Lee, 1994; Zeger et al., 1988):

- **Cluster-Robust Sandwich SEs (`mlm_robust_se()`)**: Computes
  $\hat{\mathbf{V}}_{\mathrm{rob}} = c \, \mathbf{B}^{-1} (\sum_{j=1}^J \mathbf{X}_j^\top \mathbf{V}_j^{-1} \hat{\mathbf{e}}_j \hat{\mathbf{e}}_j^\top \mathbf{V}_j^{-1} \mathbf{X}_j) \mathbf{B}^{-1}$,
  where $\mathbf{B} = \sum_{j=1}^J \mathbf{X}_j^\top \mathbf{V}_j^{-1} \mathbf{X}_j$
  is the generalized-least-squares information matrix and $c = J / (J - 1)$
  (`type = "CR1"`) or $c = 1$ (`type = "CR0"`).
- **Multiparameter Fixed-Effect Wald Tests (`mlm_wald_test()`)**: Tests
  composite hypotheses $\mathbf{c} = \mathbf{0}$ via
  $\hat{\mathbf{c}}^\top \hat{\mathbf{V}}_c^{-1} \hat{\mathbf{c}} \sim \chi^2_r$
  using either model-based or cluster-robust covariance matrices.
- **Random-Intercept and Random-Slope Reliabilities (`mlm_reliability()`)**:
  Evaluates $\mathbf{\Lambda}_j = \mathbf{I}_q - (\mathbf{I}_q + \hat{\sigma}^{-2}\hat{\mathbf{T}} \mathbf{Z}_j^\top \mathbf{Z}_j)^{-1}$
  across clusters for stable diagonal reliabilities $\hat{\lambda}_{qj} \in [0, 1)$.
- **Variance-Component LRTs (`mlm_variance_tests()`)**: Compares the full model
  against reduced models omitting one random term at a time, reporting
  boundary-adjusted $\frac{1}{2}\chi^2_{df-1} + \frac{1}{2}\chi^2_{df}$ mixture
  *p*-values (Stram & Lee, 1994).
- **Homogeneity of Level-1 Variance (`mlm_homogeneity_test()`)**: Computes
  Bartlett's $H$ statistic across clusters with $\nu_j \ge 2$ within-cluster
  degrees of freedom.
- **Population-Average Logistic Marginal Effects (`mlm_population_average()`)**:
  Applies Zeger et al.'s (1988) attenuation factor
  $(1 + (16\sqrt{3} / (15\pi))^2 \hat{\tau}_{00})^{-1/2}$ to binary logit
  unit-specific coefficients.

## Deterministic Validation Benchmarks

`mlmr` ships eight deterministic benchmark specifications covering two-level
null, random-intercept, random-slope, cross-level interaction, three-level
nested, cross-classified, longitudinal growth, and binary logistic mixed-model
workflows.

By default (`run = FALSE`), `mlm_validation_benchmarks()` checks expected
formulas and model-readiness guardrails without fitting models:

```{r benchmarks, eval = TRUE}
knitr::kable(mlmr::mlm_validation_benchmarks(run = FALSE)[, c(
  "Benchmark", "Expected Formula", "Formula Match", "Readiness Stops", "Validation Status"
)])
```

When `run = TRUE`, `mlm_validation_benchmarks()` fits all eight benchmark
models and verifies AIC agreement, fixed-effect estimates and standard errors,
variance components, Gaussian ICCs, and automated round-trip execution of the
exported R script (`Repro Code Match`) in an isolated R environment:

```{r fit-benchmarks, eval = FALSE}
mlmr::mlm_validation_benchmarks(run = TRUE)
```

## Reviewer-Facing Validation Report

To generate a complete multi-table validation object from R or download it from
the **About** tab of the Shiny app:

```{r validation-report, eval = FALSE}
report <- mlmr::mlm_validation_report()
names(report)
```
